study.question: Does a predeclared half-strength within-behavior count correction recover the loss from full correction, and is the strength response different with target-aware attention? Seven supplied trials succeeded; no failed attempts are reported. Baseline static/pooled/DIN validation AUCs are 0.6050036145/0.6102261137/0.6133619861. Seed-42 ordinary pooling and DIN bridges exactly match their respective baseline aggregate and slice metrics. Full correction loses AUC by 0.0017334134 for pooling and 0.0001905060 for DIN; Logloss worsens by 0.0000367397 and 0.0000314516. The descriptive attention-by-full-correction interaction is +0.0015429074 AUC, with no independent seed evidence. For corrected DIN, the category-match-absent slice improves AUC by 0.0003955323 but worsens Logloss by 0.0000537532 (717129 samples, 29616 positives, 687513 negatives); it cannot justify subgroup selection. First-512 diagnostics contain 468 mixed-type histories, 395 of them at least 90% pv, and indicate an active redistribution. These are selected ordered observations, not population statistics. Missing raw data, checkpoints, predictions and a local Torch runtime limit independent reproduction; successful host receipts are evidence of execution, not a fresh causal audit or a data failure.
study.hypothesis: Full inverse-count correction may remove useful relative type-frequency information or over-amplify weak rare-type events. With weights proportional to exp(s_i)/n_type(i)^alpha, alpha=0.5 retains a square-root type-frequency contribution when scores are constant while reducing multiplicity. It should recover some alpha=1 performance penalty; whether it improves on alpha=0 remains an empirical question. The flatter DIN response could reflect score adaptation, but neither the previous interaction nor a recovery identifies that explanation. This is a bounded strength/attribution follow-up to an already tested mechanism, not a new mechanism or novelty claim. Ordinary baseline-din remains incumbent until supported validation comparisons.

DIN, v4, section 4.3, equation (3) and following normalization discussion, inspected in this phase: target-conditioned activation and interest intensity are established ideas. The paper relaxes the sum-to-one constraint. Our inherited field-adapted reference uses masked softmax; the proposed intervention retains unit mass and changes relative behavior-type multiplicity. It does not restore absolute total-history intensity or claim to reproduce full DIN.

Author repository model.py attention/attention_multi_items functions (source lines approximately 200-271), read 2026-11-04 via public web: query, keys, difference and product feed an MLP, followed by masking, dimension scaling and softmax. Preserve the conflict with the paper normalization discussion rather than silently treating them as identical. Master is mutable and no commit was pinned; no exact author-implementation reproduction is claimed.

NAIS, v1, section III-A, equation (9), inspected through https://arxiv.org/html/1809.07053 (page identifies v1): a beta exponent smooths the global softmax denominator to address variable user history length. The local alpha here divides each event numerator by its visible type count to a fixed power, then normalizes across all events. It changes relative type mass while keeping total mass one. This is related normalization prior work, not the same mechanism; its recommendation results do not transfer automatically.

HMAR, v1, section 2.2 Items and Behaviors Encoding, equations (2)-(3), and Hierarchical Masked Attention, inspected: learned historical behavior indicators track per-item behavior frequency, with within/across-behavior encoders. Our proposal uses only visible per-type counts for a parameter-free event reweighting, without item-frequency features, extra encoders or multitask objectives. This is contextual nearest work, not a claim that all inverse-count methods have been exhausted.

study.proposed_difference: Implement only alpha=0.5 in two standalone modules: DIN candidate and pooling attribution control. For masked valid event i of type b, n_b is the count in the supplied causal window; use s_i - alpha*log(max(n_b,1)) before the inherited masked softmax. For pooling, s_i=0 and weights are proportional to n_b^(-alpha). Retain exact ancestor branches for alpha=0 and alpha=1 so they remain useful diagnostic counterfactuals. Empty histories return a zero summary, and padding mass is zero. Reuse the verified historical seed-42 endpoints rather than spend four duplicate trainings. This completes a descriptive attention x strength 2x3 comparison under the frozen recipe. At each new frozen checkpoint compute label-free ordinary/half/full weights on the identical first-512 batch; report all three type masses, raw per-type mean scores, summary distances, padding/sum checks, and empty/single-type invariance. Counterfactual weights/summaries are not scored model predictions or a substitute for retrained arms. The new diagnostics must return no more than 64 finite scalars, use no labels or state changes, and separate zero target fields from observed mismatches where reported. They cannot establish score compensation or rare-action utility. No additional strength, adaptive coefficient, gate, subgroup policy, optimizer or architecture branch is submitted. Literature search terms included multi-behavior target-aware attention/count normalization, DIN intensity and NAIS smoothing. Nearest-work search remains incomplete; novelty is unverified. No separate memory output is writable in this phase; these source-linked observations are recorded in the authorized proposal without changing the existing agent-r0001 record or any human-owned knowledge.
predictions: At a fixed checkpoint, pooling assigns present type b total mass proportional to n_b^(1-alpha): alpha=0 gives raw frequency, alpha=0.5 square-root frequency and alpha=1 equal present-type masses. Under constant scores across all events DIN has the same reduction. For arbitrary scores, aggregate largest-count type mass is nonincreasing with alpha; other individual types need not be monotone.

Same-checkpoint half/full corrections redistribute mixed-type histories but leave conditional within-type weights unchanged. Empty summaries remain exactly zero, and single-type summaries/weights remain equal within floating-point tolerance. Treat these as algebraic/implementation controls, not efficacy evidence.

If full correction was too strong, half correction should improve full-population validation AUC relative to alpha=1; improvement over alpha=0 is a stronger and separate performance prediction. Report Logloss alongside any ranking gain.

If learned target awareness buffers count sensitivity, the absolute half-versus-ordinary penalty should be smaller for DIN than pooling. This interaction is exploratory at seed 42 and does not establish a compensation mechanism.

A useful direction should eventually show a positive paired-seed mean AUC difference against ordinary DIN with seed variation disclosed. No significance or confidence interval will be inferred from aggregate AUCs; use paired user-cluster bootstrap only if predictions and user identities are authorized later.
falsifiers: Half correction fails to recover the full-correction AUC penalty, or ordinary DIN remains better in paired repetitions: reject the proposed performance benefit in this recipe and close the bounded correction-strength branch. One coefficient failure is not a universal mechanism refutation.
Half recovers alpha=1 loss but remains worse than ordinary: support only strength sensitivity, retain ordinary DIN, and make no model-promotion or useful-intensity mechanism claim.

Padding mass, zero empty-history summary, single-type invariance, expected type-mass reduction or endpoint source equivalence fails: treat this as an implementation/integrity failure and do not interpret model efficacy; retain failure receipts and costs.

Interaction disappears or changes direction in paired evidence: withdraw the proposed buffering explanation. Differing raw score summaries across separately trained checkpoints remain confounded by retraining.

No hard-coded numeric gain threshold, subgroup gain or withheld outcome can override full-population validation selection. Keep baseline-din unless a positive paired-seed primary difference is supported; report seed consistency/uncertainty and any Logloss cost. Freeze source/config/checkpoint suite and closest controls before one later closed assessment; no closed assessment is requested here.
